format.sourceText: Each topic: 90 min facilitated session + 45 min Q&A + 45 min timed capstone. (data/reference/expertise-training-tracks-marp.md)

modes.facilitated: A facilitator runs each module live with teams working on one shared use case per team. Facilitator notes are shown.
modes.selfPaced: One person works through each module's steps in order and answers the checkpoint questions. Progress is kept in this browser only.

modules.title: Before the workshop: readiness and pre-work
objectives: Have AI-DLC installed and passing the facilitator guide's readiness checks on every participant machine (only needed if the workshop ends with a real AI-DLC run).
Bring a one-paragraph description of the use case each team will plan.
steps: Run `aidlc config --harness <name>` in the project folder. Pass: the Runtime row reads [ok] with hook PATH ready, and the Trust row reads [ok]. (AI-DLC facilitator guide, step 1)
Run `aidlc doctor`. Pass: the summary line reads 0 problems. (step 2)
Run one throwaway stage, e.g. `/aidlc express Add a --version flag to the CLI`, and answer the first question or approval. (step 3)
Run `aidlc doctor --verbose`. Pass: a 'Hooks last fired:' row lists hook names with current times. (step 4)
Archive the throwaway intent with `/aidlc intent archive <name>`. (step 5)
Self-paced alternative: follow AI-DLC onboarding Run 1 (an Express run, stated as 15 minutes) and Run 4 (inspect aidlc/spaces/default/intents/, aidlc-state.md and audit/).
In this studio: open References and read the AI-DLC entries; open AI-DLC lifecycle and look through the five phases.
facilitatorNotes: The AI-DLC facilitator guide asks for the output of readiness steps 1, 2 and 4 from each team a week before the workshop.
The facilitator guide's pre-work is a vision note and a tech-environment note. Module 8 exports both from this studio.
If a team hits the same failure twice, the facilitator guide says to move the team to its agreed fallback harness.

modules.title: AI-DLC lifecycle, profiles and agents
objectives: Name the five phases and say which stages each profile runs.
Choose a workflow profile for the team's use case and record why.
steps: Create a blank intent (+ New intent) and give it a title.
On AI-DLC lifecycle, open each phase and read the phase purpose, the stage lead agents and the output files.
On Use-case framing, pick a workflow profile. Compare its 'Runs' and 'Skips' lists.
On AI-DLC lifecycle, select 'Create stage plan from profile'.
Add a Decision record: which profile was chosen and why.
facilitatorNotes: The facilitator guide notes that plain `/aidlc <description>` lets the assistant propose a plan; it recommends naming the scope.
The profile and scope pages count stages differently (23/30 vs 26/33 for workshop). The References page records this.
modules.capstone: Each team presents its chosen profile, the stages it runs and skips, and the Decision record.

modules.title: Ideation: intent, feasibility and scope
objectives: Write the problem, outcome, scope, exclusions and success metrics for the use case.
Record jurisdictions, data classification and risk tier, and assign accountable owners.
steps: On Use-case framing, fill in every field in Business intent and Ownership & context.
On Trust & security, initialize the control register and open GOV-01, GOV-02 and GOV-03; record an owner for each.
On Reports, download vision.md and read which sections are still empty.
facilitatorNotes: Stage 1.1 Intent Capture writes intent-statement.md and stakeholder-map.md; 1.7 Approval & Handoff writes initiative-brief.md and decision-log.md (AI-DLC artifacts reference).
NIST AI RMF MAP 1.1, MAP 1.4 and MAP 1.5 are shown on GOV-02 and in the quiz.
modules.capstone: Each team presents its vision.md: problem, outcome, in/out of scope, success metrics, risk tier.

modules.title: Inception: requirements, Units and delivery plan
objectives: Split the solution into Units of Work with explicit dependencies.
Read the dependency waves and the critical path produced by the planner.
steps: On AI-DLC lifecycle, add at least four Units with owners, scope and acceptance tests.
Mark dependencies between Units. Check the execution waves and any cycle warning.
Open stages 2.7 and 2.9 and compare their output files with what the team produced.
facilitatorNotes: AI-DLC workshop mode requires a valid Unit dependency DAG before teams claim Units.
2.8 Contract Design runs when there is more than one Unit or an externally used API (AI-DLC phases and stages).
modules.capstone: Each team shows its Unit list, dependency waves and critical-path estimate.

modules.title: Agentic architecture and threat model
objectives: Build the agent graph: nodes, edges, failure policies, tool permissions and identities.
Review every node against the OWASP agentic, OWASP LLM and ATLAS items listed for its kind, and record a status and mitigation for each.
steps: On Agentic designer, insert a pattern blueprint and adapt it, or add nodes by hand.
For every tool and agent node, fill in tool permissions and identity.
For every edge, set a failure policy and a probability.
Open each node's threat list; set each entry to mitigated, accepted or not applicable, with a mitigation.
Add at least one adversarial test scenario.
facilitatorNotes: The threat list per node kind is this studio's mapping; the item names come from the 2026 OWASP lists and ATLAS 2026.10 (see References).
modules.capstone: Each team walks through its graph and its open threat entries.

modules.title: NFRs, scale and FinOps
objectives: Enter traffic, availability and cost inputs and read the monthly projection.
Enter per-node tokens, prices and latency, run the graph simulation and read P50/P95 cost and latency per request.
Work out the error budget for the availability SLO.
steps: On NFR & cost lab, enter requests per day, peak factor, availability SLO and P95 target.
On Agentic designer, enter cost and latency inputs on every model-calling node.
On NFR & cost lab, run the graph simulation. Note mean, P50 and P95 cost and latency, and the step-cap hit rate.
Compare simulated P95 latency with the P95 target and read the error budget panel.
facilitatorNotes: All prices are user-entered. The simulation is the studio's own calculation and is not a benchmark or a quote.
3.2 NFR Requirements writes security-requirements.md and performance-requirements.md (AI-DLC artifacts reference).
modules.capstone: Each team presents cost per request (P50/P95), monthly projection, error budget and the largest cost driver node.

modules.title: Trust controls and evidence
objectives: Assess all controls with owner, status, evidence and likelihood × impact.
Read the NIST AI RMF subcategories and OWASP/ATLAS items attached to each control.
steps: On Trust & security, work through every control in each domain.
For each essential control, record evidence or an exception.
Open References and check the version and verification status of each source your controls cite.
facilitatorNotes: The coverage figure counts essential controls marked evidenced. It is the studio's calculation, not a compliance result.
ISO entries are marked unverified because iso.org blocked the automated check.
modules.capstone: Each team presents its remaining essential-control gaps and the decisions needed to close them.

modules.title: Operation: deployment, observability and feedback
objectives: Plan the Operation stages: owners, approvers and the evidence each stage should produce.
Assess the Operations controls (OPS-01 to OPS-05).
steps: On AI-DLC lifecycle, open Operation and fill owner, approver and expected evidence for each planned stage.
On Trust & security, filter by Operations and assess OPS-01 to OPS-05.
facilitatorNotes: All seven Operation stages are conditional; classic, mvp and poc run none of them (AI-DLC phases and stages).
4.7 Feedback & Optimization is the terminal stage: 'On approval, the workflow is complete.'
modules.capstone: Each team presents its Operation plan and OPS control status.

modules.title: Capstone: defend the plan and hand off to AI-DLC
objectives: Export the case report, vision.md and technical-environment.md.
Know the command that starts a real AI-DLC run from the exported vision document.
steps: On Reports, download the Markdown or print-friendly HTML report, vision.md and technical-environment.md.
Save technical-environment.md to aidlc/spaces/default/knowledge/aidlc-shared/technical-environment.md in the project (facilitator guide).
Start a real run with the command shown on Reports, e.g. `/aidlc workshop Read ./vision.md and build what it describes`.
facilitatorNotes: AI-DLC workshop mode: the integration lead completes Inception on main; each team claims one Unit, runs 3.1–3.5 and publishes; the lead pins, gates and lands each Unit (workshop-mode guide, two-day walkthrough).
The workshop profile skips Ideation and uses Standard depth with a Minimal test strategy.
modules.capstone: Each team defends its full plan: profile, scope, graph, threats, cost, controls and Operation plan.
